thread:
Andrew: hey team, Andrew here — first-week onboarding. trying to build the runtime inside Docker on mac (Intel MacBook Pro) using Docker Desktop. build hits a runtime dlopen error: 'libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file'. i thought --gpus flag would be enough. any mac-specific gotchas?

Mei: welcome Andrew! on mac Docker doesn't expose native NVIDIA drivers (macs don't have NVIDIA GPUs), so --gpus doesn’t mount libcuda on macOS. if you're using a remote linux VM or a cloud host you need to point docker at that host or use Colima/VM with GPU passthrough. are you targeting local dev or remote CI?

Andrew: local dev for quick iter iterations. i was trying to mirror CI which runs on linux with A100s. i do have an m1 VM in the cloud but wanted to avoid hopping.

Jordan: quick patterns we use: (1) for mac local dev, run the CPU-only integration or mock GPU calls (set env REDWOOD_FAKE_GPU=1) so you can iterate prompt-level logic; (2) run device-integration in a remote linux dev VM or use a cloud-based dev box; (3) if you really need linux container on mac, use SSH docker context to a linux VM that has nvidia-container-toolkit and then run with --gpus=all.

Andrew: ok that explains it — i was mistakenly assuming Docker Desktop would synthesize libcuda. where do we keep the fake GPU env/mocks?

Mei: we have a small runtime shim in infra/devtools: `tools/fake_gpu.py` and a compose override `docker-compose.dev.gpu-mock.yml`. infra-bot can link the doc.

infra-bot: Docs: https://internal.redwood/dev/docs/dev-gpu-on-mac — includes fake GPU pattern and recommended SSH docker context.

Andrew: perfect, switching to the mock flow for now and will spin up a linux dev box for device tests. thanks! :thumbsup:
